concepts.title: False friends
concepts.rule: Words that look English often mean something else: attualmente = currently, eventualmente = if need be, libreria = bookshop, parenti = relatives, educato = polite, sensibile = sensitive, morbido = soft, argomento = topic, fattoria = farm. 'To realise' is rendersi conto.
assessment: Recognises the real meaning of the most common false friends in context
Chooses the right Italian word for English 'actually', 'eventually', 'library', 'realise', 'sensible', 'argument'
Avoids anglicisms such as *ho realizzato che* in careful Italian
Translates short sentences without falling into false-friend traps

lesson.intro: Italian and English share thousands of Latin-rooted words, which is a gift until a familiar-looking word turns out to mean something else. These *falsi amici* cause some of the most noticeable mistakes English speakers make, because the sentence sounds fluent but says the wrong thing. At C1 you're expected to avoid the common ones automatically.

rules.title: Time and logic words
rules.text: *Attualmente* means **currently** (for 'actually' say *in realtà*, *in effetti*, *a dire il vero*). *Eventualmente* means **if need be, possibly** (for 'eventually' say *alla fine*, *prima o poi*). *Attuale* = current. *Effettivamente* = indeed, that's true.

examples.it: Attualmente vivo a Torino.
examples.en: I currently live in Turin.

examples.it: Sembra semplice, ma in realtà è complicato.
examples.en: It looks simple, but actually it's complicated.

examples.it: Eventualmente possiamo spostare la riunione a giovedì.
examples.en: If need be, we can move the meeting to Thursday.

examples.it: Alla fine ha accettato.
examples.en: Eventually he accepted.

rules.title: People and character
rules.text: *Parenti* = **relatives** (parents = *genitori*). *Educato* = **polite, well-mannered** (educated = *istruito, colto*). *Sensibile* = **sensitive** (sensible = *sensato* for things, *giudizioso, assennato* for people). *Simpatico* = **likeable, nice** (sympathetic = *comprensivo, solidale*). *Morbido* = **soft** (morbid = *morboso*).

examples.it: A Natale vengono tutti i parenti.
examples.en: All the relatives come at Christmas.

examples.it: Tuo figlio è molto educato: saluta sempre.
examples.en: Your son is very polite: he always says hello.

examples.it: È una ragazza sensibile, si commuove facilmente.
examples.en: She's a sensitive girl, she's easily moved.

rules.title: Places and things
rules.text: Places and objects are a classic trap, and some mistakes (*preservativo*!) can be embarrassing.

examples.it: Ho comprato il romanzo in libreria e l'ho letto in biblioteca.
examples.en: I bought the novel at the bookshop and read it at the library.

examples.it: Hanno litigato per un argomento banale.
examples.en: They argued about a trivial topic.

rules.title: Verbs
rules.text: *Realizzare* = **carry out, achieve, make real** (*realizzare un progetto*). For 'realise' use *rendersi conto*, *accorgersi*: *realizzare* in that sense is a widespread anglicism, best avoided in careful Italian. *Pretendere* = **demand, expect** (pretend = *fingere, fare finta*). *Assistere a* = **witness, watch** (assist = *aiutare*). *Attendere* = **wait** (attend = *frequentare, partecipare a*). *Confrontare* = **compare** (confront = *affrontare*). *Assumere* = **hire, take on** (assume = *supporre*). *Controllare* = **check** (control = *gestire, dominare*).

examples.it: Mi sono reso conto di aver sbagliato.
examples.en: I realised I'd made a mistake.

examples.it: Hanno realizzato il progetto in sei mesi.
examples.en: They carried out the project in six months.

examples.it: Pretendo delle scuse.
examples.en: I demand an apology.

examples.it: Ho partecipato al convegno.
examples.en: I attended the conference.

mistakes.why: *Attualmente* means 'currently', not 'actually'.

mistakes.right: Mi sono reso conto che era tardi.
mistakes.why: 'Realise' (become aware) is *rendersi conto*. *Realizzare* means 'carry out'; the 'realise' meaning is an anglicism.
A *libreria* sells books; a *biblioteca* lends them and has reading rooms.

mistakes.wrong: I miei parenti vivono a Londra. (= my mum and dad)
mistakes.right: I miei genitori vivono a Londra.
mistakes.why: *Parenti* are relatives in general; parents are *genitori*.

mistakes.wrong: È molto educato, ha due lauree.
mistakes.right: È molto istruito, ha due lauree.
mistakes.why: *Educato* means polite. 'Educated' is *istruito* or *colto*.

tips: When an Italian word looks exactly like English, pause and check it in a monolingual dictionary (Treccani, Garzanti) before using it in writing.
Learn false friends in pairs: *attualmente* ≠ actually → *in realtà*; *eventualmente* ≠ eventually → *alla fine*.
Some anglicisms (*realizzare* = realise, *evidenze* = evidence) are spreading in journalism. Recognise them, but prefer the traditional word in careful writing.

exercises.prompt: Mio fratello lavora in una ___: vende romanzi, saggi e guide di viaggio.

optionWhy.1: A *biblioteca* lends books (library); it doesn't sell them.
optionWhy.2: *Libraria* isn't a noun (it's the feminine of the adjective *librario*).

exercises.explanation: *Libreria* = bookshop (or bookcase). Library = *biblioteca*.
exercises.en: My brother works in a bookshop: he sells novels, essays and travel guides.

exercises.prompt: A Natale vengono a pranzo tutti i miei ___: zii, cugini, nonni.

optionWhy.1: *Genitori* are just your mother and father, but here we have uncles, cousins and grandparents.
optionWhy.2: *Relativo* is an adjective ('relative to'), not a noun for family members.

exercises.explanation: *Parenti* = relatives. Parents = *genitori*.
exercises.en: At Christmas all my relatives come for lunch: uncles, cousins, grandparents.

exercises.prompt: Sembra un lavoro facile, ma ___ (actually) è molto complicato.

traps.why: *Attualmente* means 'currently'. 'Actually' (in fact) is *in realtà*.
*Attuale* means 'current'. 'Actually' is *in realtà*.

exercises.explanation: 'Actually' = *in realtà / in effetti / a dire il vero*. *Attualmente* = currently.
exercises.en: It looks like an easy job, but actually it's very complicated.

exercises.prompt: What does *eventualmente* mean here? «Eventualmente possiamo spostare la riunione a giovedì.»

optionWhy.0: 'Eventually' (in the end) is *alla fine* or *prima o poi*.

exercises.explanation: *Eventualmente* = if need be, possibly, should the case arise.
exercises.en: If need be, we can move the meeting to Thursday.

exercises.prompt: Il vostro bambino è molto ___ (polite): saluta sempre e dice grazie.

traps.why: *Istruito* means 'educated' (well-schooled). Polite is *educato*.
*Colto* means 'cultured, well-read'. Polite is *educato*.

exercises.explanation: *Educato* = polite, well brought up. Educated = *istruito / colto*.
exercises.en: Your child is very polite: he always says hello and thank you.

exercises.prompt: This sweater is really soft.

traps.why: *Morboso* means 'morbid'. Soft is *morbido* (or *soffice*).

exercises.explanation: *Morbido* = soft. Morbid = *morboso*.
exercises.en: This sweater is really soft.

exercises.prompt: How do you say 'I realised I had forgotten my keys' in careful Italian?
options: Ho realizzato di aver dimenticato le chiavi.
Mi sono reso conto di aver dimenticato le chiavi.
Mi sono realizzato di aver dimenticato le chiavi.

optionWhy.0: You'll hear it, but *realizzare* = 'realise' is an anglicism. Its core meaning is 'carry out, achieve'. Use *rendersi conto*.
optionWhy.2: *Realizzarsi* means 'to fulfil oneself' (*si è realizzato nel lavoro*), not 'realise'.

exercises.explanation: Realise (become aware) = *rendersi conto* or *accorgersi*.
exercises.en: I realised I had forgotten my keys.

exercises.prompt: Il nuovo ponte è stato ___ (carried out, built) in soli due anni.
exercises.explanation: Here *realizzare* is used in its genuine Italian sense: to carry out, make, build.
exercises.en: The new bridge was built in just two years.

exercises.prompt: She's a very sensitive person.

traps.why: *Sensato* means 'sensible, reasonable'. Sensitive is *sensibile*.

exercises.explanation: *Sensibile* = sensitive. Sensible = *sensato / giudizioso*.
exercises.en: She's a very sensitive person.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence means 'He's a sensible guy'?
exercises.explanation: A sensible person is *giudizioso*, *assennato* or *con la testa sulle spalle*. A sensible decision is *sensata*.
exercises.en: He's a sensible guy.

exercises.prompt: They had an argument about money.
answers: (Hanno litigato|Hanno avuto una discussione|Hanno avuto un litigio|Hanno discusso) (per i soldi|per soldi|per questioni di soldi|a causa dei soldi|sui soldi)

traps.why: *Argomento* means 'topic'. A quarrel is *un litigio* or *una discussione*; the verb is *litigare*.

exercises.explanation: Argument (quarrel) = *litigio / discussione*; to argue = *litigare*. *Argomento* = topic.
exercises.en: They had an argument about money.

exercises.prompt: Mio padre lavora in una ___ (factory) di automobili vicino a Torino.

traps.why: *Fattoria* is a farm. A factory is a *fabbrica* (or *stabilimento*).

exercises.explanation: Factory = *fabbrica*. *Fattoria* = farm.
exercises.en: My father works in a car factory near Turin.

exercises.prompt: «Pretendo una risposta entro domani.» This means:
options: I'm pretending to have an answer by tomorrow.
I demand an answer by tomorrow.
I intend to give an answer by tomorrow.
exercises.explanation: *Pretendere* = to demand, to expect (as a right).
exercises.en: I demand an answer by tomorrow.

exercises.instruction: Replace the anglicism with natural Italian (use rendersi conto, accorgersi or capire).
exercises.prompt: Ho realizzato che era troppo tardi.
answers: Mi sono (reso|resa) conto che era troppo tardi
Mi sono (accorto|accorta) che era troppo tardi
Ho capito che era troppo tardi

traps.why: Avoid *realizzare* for 'realise' in careful Italian: use *rendersi conto* or *accorgersi*.

exercises.explanation: *Mi sono reso/a conto che…* is the standard way to say 'I realised that…'. Note the auxiliary *essere* with the reflexive.
exercises.en: I realised it was too late.

exercises.prompt: I attended the conference last week.
answers: La settimana scorsa ho (partecipato|assistito) (al convegno|alla conferenza)
Ho (partecipato|assistito) (al convegno|alla conferenza) la settimana scorsa
La settimana scorsa sono andato (al convegno|alla conferenza)
La settimana scorsa sono andata (al convegno|alla conferenza)

traps.why: *Attendere* means 'to wait for'. To attend a conference is *partecipare a* (or *assistere a* as a listener).
*Frequentare* is for attending regularly (a school, a course). For a single event use *partecipare a*.

exercises.explanation: Attend an event = *partecipare a* / *assistere a*. *Attendere* = to wait.
exercises.en: I attended the conference last week.

exercises.prompt: A friend asks what you do. Say that you are currently working in a bookshop.
answers: (Attualmente|Al momento|In questo momento|Adesso|Ora|Per ora) (lavoro|sto lavorando) in una libreria
(Lavoro|Sto lavorando) in una libreria (attualmente|al momento|in questo momento|adesso|ora|per ora)

traps.why: A *biblioteca* is a library. A bookshop is a *libreria*.
'Currently' is the adverb *attualmente* (or *al momento*).

exercises.explanation: *Attualmente* = currently; *libreria* = bookshop.
exercises.en: I'm currently working in a bookshop.

exercises.prompt: Non è stato per niente ___ (understanding): quando gli ho raccontato i miei problemi, mi ha riso in faccia.

traps.why: *Simpatico* means 'likeable, nice', not 'sympathetic'. Understanding, supportive = *comprensivo*.
*Comprensibile* means 'understandable' (of a thing). An understanding person is *comprensivo*.

exercises.explanation: Sympathetic, understanding = *comprensivo*. *Simpatico* = likeable; *comprensibile* = understandable.
exercises.en: He wasn't understanding at all: when I told him my problems, he laughed in my face.

exercises.prompt: Currently my relatives live on a farm.
answers: (Attualmente|Al momento|Adesso|Ora|Oggi) i miei parenti (vivono|abitano) in una fattoria
I miei parenti (vivono|abitano) (attualmente|al momento|adesso|ora) in una fattoria

traps.why: Relatives = *parenti*. *Relativo* is an adjective.
*Genitori* are parents only; relatives in general are *parenti*.
A *fabbrica* is a factory. A farm is a *fattoria*.
'Currently' is *attualmente / al momento*; *in realtà* means 'actually'.

exercises.explanation: Three false friends in one: *attualmente* = currently, *parenti* = relatives, *fattoria* = farm.
exercises.en: Currently my relatives live on a farm.

concepts.title: Core collocations with fare, dare, prendere, avere
concepts.rule: Italian pairs nouns with light verbs differently from English: prendere una decisione, fare una domanda / una foto / la doccia, avere senso / luogo / fretta, dare fastidio / una mano / retta. Learn them as fixed chunks.
assessment: Uses the right light verb (fare, prendere, dare, avere) with common nouns
Avoids English calques such as *fare una decisione*, *prendere una foto*, *fa senso*
Understands figurative collocations (prendere in giro, dare retta, fare caso a, fare finta)
Uses these collocations spontaneously in short spoken and written answers

lesson.intro: English builds countless expressions with make, take, have and give, and Italian does the same with *fare, prendere, dare, avere*, but the pairings rarely match. Translating word for word gives *~~fare una decisione~~* or *~~prendere una foto~~*, which Italians understand but immediately notice. Learn each noun together with its verb, as one chunk.

rules.title: Fare: activities, routines and many English 'take / have / ask'
rules.text: *fare una domanda* (ask a question), *fare una foto* (take a photo), *fare una passeggiata / due passi* (go for a walk), *fare colazione* (have breakfast), *fare la doccia* (have a shower), *fare una pausa* (take a break), *fare la fila* (queue), *fare attenzione* (pay attention), *fare caso a* (notice), *fare finta di* (pretend), *fare a meno di* (do without), *fare fatica a* (struggle to), *fare paura* (be scary).

examples.it: Posso farti una domanda?
examples.en: Can I ask you a question?

examples.it: Non ho fatto caso all'ora.
examples.en: I didn't notice the time.

examples.it: Non riesco a fare a meno del caffè.
examples.en: I can't do without coffee.

rules.title: Prendere: decisions and things you take in
rules.text: *prendere una decisione* (make a decision), *prendere un caffè* (have a coffee), *prendere appunti* (take notes), *prendere il sole* (sunbathe), *prendere freddo* (catch a chill), *prendere in giro* (tease, make fun of, con), *prendere sul serio* (take seriously), *prendere una multa* (get a fine), *prendere l'iniziativa*.

examples.it: Dobbiamo prendere una decisione entro venerdì.
examples.en: We have to make a decision by Friday.

examples.it: Mi stai prendendo in giro?
examples.en: Are you pulling my leg?

rules.title: Dare: giving something abstract
rules.text: *dare fastidio* (bother; *fare fastidio* is also common), *dare una mano* (lend a hand), *dare un'occhiata* (have a look), *dare retta a* (listen to, heed), *dare per scontato* (take for granted), *dare la colpa a* (blame), *dare ragione a* (agree someone is right), *dare un passaggio* (give a lift), *dare un esame* (sit an exam: student language; formally *sostenere un esame*).

examples.it: Ti dà fastidio se apro la finestra?
examples.en: Do you mind if I open the window?

examples.it: Dammi retta: non partire stasera.
examples.en: Listen to me: don't leave tonight.

rules.title: Avere: states, needs and events
rules.text: *avere senso* (make sense), *avere voglia di* (feel like), *avere bisogno di* (need), *avere fretta* (be in a hurry), *avere ragione / torto* (be right / wrong), *avere luogo* (take place, formal), *avere a che fare con* (have to do with, deal with), *avere fame / sete / sonno / caldo / freddo / paura*.

examples.it: Questa frase non ha senso.
examples.en: This sentence doesn't make sense.

examples.it: La cerimonia avrà luogo in Duomo.
examples.en: The ceremony will take place in the cathedral.

mistakes.why: Decisions are *taken* in Italian: *prendere una decisione*.
*Fare senso* means 'to gross out' (*il sangue mi fa senso*). Some young speakers say *fa senso* for 'makes sense', but it's non-standard.
You *fare* a question, or simply *chiedere una cosa*.

mistakes.wrong: Il concerto prende posto in piazza.
mistakes.right: Il concerto ha luogo (si svolge) in piazza.
mistakes.why: 'Take place' = *avere luogo* or *svolgersi*. *Prendere posto* = take a seat.
Being right is something you *have*: *avere ragione*.

tips: Memorise verb and noun as one block: *prendere-una-decisione*, *fare-una-domanda*.
For activities and routines, *fare* is the safest bet (*fare sport, fare la spesa, fare un giro*).
*Dare un esame* is everyday student talk; in formal writing use *sostenere un esame*.

exercises.prompt: Scusi, posso ___ una domanda?

traps.why: *Chiedere una domanda* is a calque. You *fare* (or, formally, *porre*) a question.
*Domandare una domanda* is redundant. Use *fare una domanda*.

exercises.explanation: Ask a question = *fare una domanda* (formal: *porre*).
exercises.en: Excuse me, may I ask a question?

exercises.prompt: Dobbiamo ___ una decisione entro venerdì.

traps.why: Decisions are taken, not made, in Italian: *prendere una decisione*.

exercises.explanation: Make a decision = *prendere una decisione*.
exercises.en: We have to make a decision by Friday.

exercises.prompt: Questa frase non ___ senso.

optionWhy.0: *Fare senso* means 'to gross out' (*il sangue mi fa senso*). 'Make sense' = *avere senso*.
optionWhy.2: *Dare senso* = to give meaning (*dare un senso alla vita*), not 'make sense'.

exercises.explanation: Make sense = *avere senso*.
exercises.en: This sentence doesn't make sense.

exercises.prompt: Aspettami cinque minuti: mi ___ una doccia veloce e arrivo.

optionWhy.1: *Prendere una doccia* is a calque from English/French; standard Italian uses *fare la doccia*.
optionWhy.2: *Avere una doccia* is a calque of 'have a shower'.

exercises.explanation: Have a shower = *fare la doccia* (*farsi una doccia* in speech).
exercises.en: Wait five minutes for me: I'll have a quick shower and I'll be there.

exercises.prompt: Non ___ finta di niente: so che hai letto il mio messaggio!

traps.why: Right verb, but the negative *tu* imperative is *non* + infinitive: *non fare*.
Pretend = *fare finta (di)*.

exercises.explanation: *Fare finta di* = to pretend. Negative tu imperative: *non fare*.
exercises.en: Don't pretend nothing's happened: I know you've read my message!

exercises.prompt: Stasera non ho ___ di uscire: resto a casa.

traps.why: *Avere voglia di* is the natural way to say 'feel like'.
*Avere bisogno di* = to need. 'Feel like' = *avere voglia di*.

exercises.explanation: Feel like (doing) = *avere voglia di*.
exercises.en: I don't feel like going out tonight: I'm staying in.

exercises.prompt: Let's take a short walk before dinner.
answers: Facciamo due passi prima di cena
Prima di cena facciamo due passi
exercises.explanation: *Fare due passi* = go for a short walk (lit. 'take two steps').
exercises.en: Let's take a short walk before dinner.

exercises.prompt: Pay attention to the traffic!

traps.why: You don't *pay* attention in Italian: *fare (or prestare) attenzione*.

exercises.explanation: Pay attention = *fare attenzione* / *prestare attenzione* / *stare attento*.
exercises.en: Pay attention to the traffic!

exercises.prompt: Mi puoi ___ una mano a spostare il divano?

traps.why: Lend a hand = *dare una mano*.
Lend a hand = *dare una mano*.

exercises.explanation: *Dare una mano* = lend a hand, help.
exercises.en: Can you give me a hand moving the sofa?

exercises.prompt: «Mi stai prendendo in giro?» means:
options: Are you taking me for a ride in the car?

optionWhy.0: A ride is *un giro* or *un passaggio*, but *prendere in giro* is figurative.
optionWhy.2: Picking someone up is *passare a prendere*.

exercises.explanation: *Prendere in giro* = to tease, make fun of, or con.
exercises.en: Are you pulling my leg?

exercises.prompt: Se mi avessi ___ retta, adesso non saresti in questo guaio.

traps.why: Listen to / heed someone = *dare retta a qualcuno*.

exercises.explanation: *Dare retta a* = listen to, follow someone's advice.
exercises.en: If you'd listened to me, you wouldn't be in this mess now.

exercises.prompt: La cerimonia ___ luogo sabato alle undici in municipio.

traps.why: 'Take place' is not *prendere luogo*: use *avere luogo* (or *si svolgerà*).
'Take place' = *avere luogo*.

exercises.explanation: Take place = *avere luogo* (or *svolgersi*).
exercises.en: The ceremony will take place on Saturday at eleven at the town hall.

exercises.prompt: Hai ___ caso a come ci guardava quel signore?

traps.why: Notice = *fare caso a*.

exercises.explanation: *Fare caso a* = to notice, pay attention to.
exercises.en: Did you notice how that man was looking at us?

exercises.prompt: Non posso vivere senza caffè.
answers: Non posso fare a meno del caffè
Non riesco a fare a meno del caffè

traps.why: *Fare a meno di* already means 'do without', so drop *senza*.
*Di* + *il* merges: *fare a meno del caffè*.

exercises.explanation: *Fare a meno di* + noun = do without. *Di + il caffè* → *del caffè*.
exercises.en: I can't do without coffee.

exercises.prompt: I took a lot of photos in Rome.
answers: Ho fatto (molte|tante|un sacco di|parecchie) (foto|fotografie) a Roma
A Roma ho fatto (molte|tante|un sacco di|parecchie) (foto|fotografie)

traps.why: Photos are *made* in Italian: *fare una foto*.
*Scattare una foto* is also correct, but here practise *fare*: *ho fatto molte foto*.

exercises.explanation: Take a photo = *fare una foto* (also *scattare*).
exercises.en: I took a lot of photos in Rome.

exercises.prompt: You bump into a friend but must run. Say: 'Sorry, I'm in a hurry!'
answers: (Scusa|Scusami|Mi dispiace) (ho fretta|ho molta fretta|vado di fretta|vado di corsa|sono di fretta|sono di corsa)

traps.why: Be in a hurry = *avere fretta* (or *andare di fretta*).
*Mi sbrigo* means 'I'll hurry up'. To say you're in a hurry: *ho fretta*.

exercises.explanation: Be in a hurry = *avere fretta* / *andare di fretta*.
exercises.en: Sorry, I'm in a hurry!

exercises.prompt: Don't take it for granted that everyone agrees: ask a question at the meeting.
answers: Non dare per scontato che (tutti siano d'accordo|siano tutti d'accordo)[,] fai una domanda alla riunione
Non dare per scontato che (tutti siano d'accordo|siano tutti d'accordo)[,] fa' una domanda alla riunione

traps.why: Take for granted = *dare per scontato*.
*Dare per scontato che* is followed by the subjunctive: *siano*.
Ask a question = *fare una domanda*.

exercises.explanation: *Dare per scontato che* + subjunctive; *fare una domanda*. Negative tu imperative = *non* + infinitive.
exercises.en: Don't take it for granted that everyone agrees: ask a question at the meeting.

exercises.prompt: Describe a difficult decision you made. Use at least three collocations with fare, dare, prendere or avere (e.g. prendere una decisione, avere senso, dare retta, fare fatica).

rubric.label: Uses prendere una decisione
rubric.hint: Decisions are taken: *ho preso una decisione*.

rubric.label: Uses a collocation with dare or fare
rubric.hint: Try *ho fatto fatica a…* or *ho dato retta a…*.

exercises.model: Due anni fa ho dovuto prendere una decisione difficile: lasciare il lavoro e trasferirmi a Bologna. All'inizio ho fatto fatica ad accettarlo, perché avevo paura di sbagliare. Poi ho dato retta a mia sorella, che mi ha detto che restare non aveva senso. Oggi le do ragione: è stata la scelta giusta.
exercises.explanation: A good answer recycles fixed chunks: *prendere una decisione*, *fare fatica a*, *avere paura*, *dare retta a*, *non avere senso*.

concepts.title: Advanced collocations (porre fine, prendere atto…)
concepts.rule: Formal Italian uses precise verb–noun pairs with fixed prepositions: porre fine a, prendere atto di, svolgere un ruolo, trarre vantaggio da, recare danno a, sollevare una questione, tenere conto di. Avoid calques like indirizzare un problema or prendere vantaggio.
assessment: Uses formal verb–noun collocations (porre fine a, prendere atto di, svolgere un ruolo, trarre vantaggio da) with the right preposition
Replaces generic verbs (fare, mettere, dire) with precise collocations in formal writing
Avoids calques such as *indirizzare un problema*, *alzare una questione*, *prendere vantaggio*
Pairs nouns with natural adjectives (netto calo, accesa discussione, ampio consenso)

lesson.intro: At C1 the difference between correct and *convincing* Italian is often collocation. News, reports, formal emails and essays prefer precise verb–noun pairs like *porre fine a*, *prendere atto di*, *svolgere un ruolo*, where everyday speech would just use *fare* or *mettere*. Using them signals a sophisticated register; calquing English (*indirizzare un problema*) signals the opposite.

rules.title: Porre, sollevare, avanzare, muovere: putting things forward
rules.text: *porre fine a* (put an end to), *porre rimedio a* (remedy), *porre le basi per* (lay the foundations for), *porre una domanda / una condizione*; *sollevare una questione / un problema / obiezioni / dubbi* (raise); *avanzare una proposta / un'ipotesi / una richiesta* (put forward); *muovere una critica / un'accusa* (level a criticism / an accusation).

examples.it: L'accordo ha posto fine a dieci anni di conflitto.
examples.en: The agreement put an end to ten years of conflict.

examples.it: Alcuni consiglieri hanno sollevato dubbi sui costi.
examples.en: Some councillors raised doubts about the costs.

rules.title: Prendere, tenere, fare fronte: dealing with situations
rules.text: *prendere atto di* (formally acknowledge), *prendere provvedimenti / misure* (take measures; also *adottare misure*), *prendere in considerazione* (consider), *tenere conto di* (take into account), *fare fronte a* (cope with, meet: *spese, un'emergenza*), *affrontare un problema* (tackle a problem).

examples.it: Prendiamo atto della sua decisione.
examples.en: We acknowledge your decision.

examples.it: Il comune non riesce a far fronte alle spese.
examples.en: The council can't meet its expenses.

rules.title: Svolgere, ricoprire, trarre, recare: roles, benefits and harm
rules.text: *svolgere un ruolo / un'attività / un compito / un'indagine* (play a role, carry out); *ricoprire una carica* (hold an office); *trarre vantaggio / beneficio / profitto da* (benefit from), *trarre le conclusioni*, *trarre ispirazione da*; *recare (arrecare) danno / disturbo a* (cause harm / inconvenience); *commettere un errore / un reato*; *correre un rischio*.

examples.it: La scuola svolge un ruolo fondamentale.
examples.en: School plays a fundamental role.

examples.it: Ci scusiamo per il disturbo arrecato.
examples.en: We apologise for any inconvenience caused.

rules.title: Adjective + noun pairs
rules.text: Native writers reach for these pairings automatically; using them makes a text sound idiomatic.

examples.it: Le vendite hanno registrato un netto calo.
examples.en: Sales recorded a sharp drop.

rules.title: Calques to avoid
rules.text: *~~indirizzare un problema~~* → *affrontare*; *~~alzare una questione~~* → *sollevare*; *~~prendere vantaggio~~* → *trarre vantaggio da* / *approfittare di*; *~~prendere un rischio~~* → *correre un rischio*. *Giocare un ruolo* is frequent in journalism but considered an anglicism: prefer *svolgere / avere / ricoprire un ruolo*.

examples.it: Bisogna affrontare il problema alla radice.
examples.en: We need to address the problem at its root.

mistakes.why: *Indirizzare* = to address a letter or direct something. 'Address a problem' = *affrontare*.
Questions and objections are *sollevate*.

mistakes.right: Hanno approfittato della situazione. / Hanno tratto vantaggio dalla situazione.
mistakes.why: *Prendere vantaggio* doesn't exist in this sense.
Risks are *run*: *correre un rischio*.
*Prendere atto* needs *di*.

tips: Learn the preposition with the chunk: porre fine **a**, prendere atto **di**, trarre vantaggio **da**, recare danno **a**, tenere conto **di**, fare fronte **a**.
Read one Italian news article a day and highlight verb–noun pairs; note which verb a journalist chooses instead of *fare*.
In conversation these can sound stiff: with friends, *mettere fine a* and *pensarci* are perfectly fine.

exercises.prompt: Il governo vuole ___ fine alla crisi entro l'estate.

traps.why: Put an end to = *porre (mettere) fine a*.
Put an end to = *porre fine a*.

exercises.explanation: *Porre fine a* (formal) / *mettere fine a* (neutral) = put an end to.
exercises.en: The government wants to put an end to the crisis by the summer.

exercises.instruction: Choose the verb preferred in careful written Italian.
exercises.prompt: La ricerca ___ un ruolo fondamentale nello sviluppo del Paese.

optionWhy.1: *Giocare un ruolo* is a calque of 'play a role'. Common in journalism, but careful writers prefer *svolgere*, *avere* or *ricoprire*.
optionWhy.2: *Fare un ruolo* is colloquial (an actor *fa la parte di…*).
optionWhy.3: *Prendere un ruolo* doesn't mean 'play a role'.

exercises.explanation: *Svolgere un ruolo* = play a role.
exercises.en: Research plays a fundamental role in the country's development.

exercises.prompt: Prendiamo ___ della sua decisione e procederemo di conseguenza.

traps.why: *Prendere nota* = to note down. It's possible, but *prendere atto* is the formal way to say 'acknowledge'.
*Tenere conto di* = take into account; but here the verb is *prendere*: *prendere atto di*.

exercises.explanation: *Prendere atto di* = formally acknowledge (often a decision you don't like).
exercises.en: We acknowledge your decision and will act accordingly.

exercises.prompt: Molte aziende hanno ___ vantaggio dalla crisi dei concorrenti.

traps.why: *Prendere vantaggio* is a calque. Use *trarre vantaggio da* (or *approfittare di*).
*Avere un vantaggio* = to have an advantage; benefit from = *trarre vantaggio da*.

exercises.explanation: *Trarre vantaggio da* = benefit from. Past participle of *trarre*: *tratto*.
exercises.en: Many companies benefited from their competitors' crisis.

exercises.prompt: La cattiva gestione ha ___ grave danno all'immagine dell'azienda.

optionWhy.2: *Svolgere* goes with *un ruolo, un compito, un'attività*.

exercises.explanation: *Recare (arrecare) danno a* = cause harm to.
exercises.en: Bad management has seriously damaged the company's image.

exercises.prompt: Durante il consiglio comunale, la sindaca ha ___ una questione delicata: chi pagherà i lavori?

traps.why: *Alzare* is literal (raise a hand). A question or issue is *sollevata* (or *posta*).
*Aumentare* means increase. Raise an issue = *sollevare una questione*.

exercises.explanation: *Sollevare una questione* = raise an issue.
exercises.en: During the council meeting, the mayor raised a delicate issue: who will pay for the works?

exercises.prompt: Le vendite del primo trimestre hanno registrato un ___ calo.

optionWhy.1: *Alto* goes with levels (*un alto livello*), not with a drop.

exercises.explanation: *Un netto calo* = a sharp drop (also *forte, drastico*).
exercises.en: First-quarter sales recorded a sharp drop.

exercises.prompt: La scuola ha preso ___ severi contro il bullismo.

traps.why: 'Take steps' is not *prendere passi*: say *prendere provvedimenti / misure*.
'Take action' = *intervenire* or *prendere provvedimenti*; *prendere azioni* is a calque.

exercises.explanation: *Prendere provvedimenti / misure* = take measures, take action.
exercises.en: The school took strict measures against bullying.

exercises.prompt: We must take this into account.

traps.why: Take into account = *tenere conto di* (with *ne*: *tenerne conto*).
It's *tenere conto*, not *prendere conto*.

exercises.explanation: *Tenere conto di* → with a pronoun, *tenerne conto*. Or *prendere in considerazione*.
exercises.en: We must take this into account.

exercises.prompt: We must draw conclusions from these data.
answers: Dobbiamo trarre le conclusioni da questi dati
Da questi dati dobbiamo trarre le conclusioni
exercises.explanation: *Trarre le conclusioni (da)* = draw conclusions (from).
exercises.en: We must draw conclusions from these data.

exercises.instruction: Rewrite more formally using 'porre fine a'.
exercises.prompt: Il nuovo accordo ha fatto finire la guerra.
answers: Il nuovo accordo ha posto fine alla guerra

traps.why: *Mettere fine a* is correct but neutral; the task asks for the formal *porre fine a*: *ha posto fine*.
*Porre fine* needs *a*: *a + la guerra* → *alla guerra*.
The past participle of *porre* is *posto*.

exercises.explanation: *Porre fine a* → passato prossimo *ha posto fine alla…*
exercises.en: The new agreement put an end to the war.

exercises.prompt: Dal 2019 la dottoressa Neri ___ la carica di direttrice generale.

traps.why: 'Hold an office' isn't *tenere*: say *ricoprire (rivestire, occupare) una carica*.
Offices are held: *ricoprire una carica*.

exercises.explanation: *Ricoprire una carica* = hold an office.
exercises.en: Since 2019 Dr Neri has held the post of director general.

exercises.instruction: Which expression is NOT natural Italian?
exercises.prompt: Il nuovo assessore deve ___ il problema del traffico.

optionWhy.0: *Affrontare un problema* is natural: you're looking for the odd one out.

exercises.explanation: *Indirizzare un problema* is a calque of 'address a problem'. Use *affrontare*.
exercises.en: The new councillor must tackle the traffic problem.

exercises.prompt: This decision could cause serious damage to the company.
answers: Questa decisione potrebbe (recare|arrecare|causare|provocare) (gravi danni|un grave danno|danni gravi) (all'azienda|alla società)
Questa decisione potrebbe danneggiare gravemente (l'azienda|la società)

traps.why: Correct-ish in speech, but formally use *recare / arrecare / causare danno a*.
*Dannare* = to damn. Use *recare danno a* or *danneggiare*.

exercises.explanation: *Recare / arrecare danno a* = cause harm to (formal).
exercises.en: This decision could cause serious damage to the company.

exercises.prompt: The minister raised a question that nobody had considered.
answers: (Il ministro|La ministra) ha (sollevato|posto) una questione che nessuno aveva (considerato|preso in considerazione|valutato)

traps.why: Raise an issue = *sollevare una questione*.
*Questione* (issue) fits better than *domanda* (a question asked) here.

exercises.explanation: *Sollevare / porre una questione*; trapassato *aveva considerato*.
exercises.en: The minister raised a question that nobody had considered.

exercises.instruction: Answer aloud (or type) in Italian, formal register.
exercises.prompt: At a meeting, tell the client (Lei): 'We acknowledge your proposal and will take it into account.'
answers: Prendiamo atto della (sua|Sua|vostra) proposta e (ne terremo conto|la terremo in considerazione|la prenderemo in considerazione|la valuteremo)

traps.why: *Prendere atto* needs *di*: *della sua proposta*.
Take into account = *tenerne conto*.

exercises.explanation: *Prendere atto di* + *tenerne conto* / *prenderla in considerazione*.
exercises.en: We acknowledge your proposal and will take it into account.

exercises.prompt: You are writing a short report for your company about a problem (e.g. delays, rising costs). Use at least three advanced collocations: porre fine a, prendere atto di, svolgere un ruolo, trarre vantaggio da, recare danno a, sollevare una questione, fare fronte a, prendere provvedimenti.

rubric.label: Uses at least three advanced collocations
rubric.hint: Combine, for example, *sollevare una questione*, *prendere provvedimenti*, *porre fine a*.

rubric.label: Uses a formal linking word
rubric.hint: Link your sentences with *pertanto*, *tuttavia* or *in questo modo*.

exercises.model: Negli ultimi mesi i ritardi nelle consegne hanno recato danno all'immagine dell'azienda. Durante l'ultima riunione il responsabile logistico ha sollevato la questione dei fornitori. Prendiamo atto delle difficoltà, ma è necessario prendere provvedimenti: proponiamo di cambiare fornitore per porre fine a questa situazione. In questo modo potremo anche trarre vantaggio da prezzi più competitivi.
exercises.explanation: A strong report chains several formal collocations: *recare danno a*, *sollevare una questione*, *prendere atto di*, *prendere provvedimenti*, *porre fine a*, *trarre vantaggio da*.

concepts.title: Everyday idioms
concepts.rule: Everyday idioms are fixed chunks with vivid images: essere al verde, costare un occhio della testa, non vedere l'ora di, avere le mani bucate, in bocca al lupo (– crepi!). Don't change their words, and keep informal ones out of formal contexts.
assessment: Understands common everyday idioms in context
Uses idioms in their fixed form (right noun, preposition, singular or plural)
Responds appropriately to ritual expressions (In bocca al lupo! – Crepi!)
Chooses idioms that suit the register of the situation

lesson.intro: Italians use idioms constantly in everyday conversation, often built on a vivid image: wolves, clouds, bread, the Pope. You don't need hundreds, but you do need to understand the common ones instantly and use a few naturally. Most are informal or neutral, so match them to the situation.

rules.title: Money
rules.text: *essere al verde* (be broke; lit. 'be at the green', from the green base of old candles), *costare un occhio della testa* (cost an arm and a leg; lit. 'an eye from your head'), *avere le mani bucate* (spend money like water; lit. 'have holes in your hands'), *spendere e spandere* (splash out).

examples.it: Fino a fine mese sono al verde.
examples.en: I'm broke until the end of the month.

examples.it: Quella macchina costa un occhio della testa.
examples.en: That car costs an arm and a leg.

rules.title: Feelings and moods
rules.text: *non vedere l'ora di* (can't wait to; lit. 'not see the hour'), *avere un diavolo per capello* (be furious; lit. 'a devil for every hair'), *avere la luna storta* (be in a bad mood; lit. 'have a crooked moon'), *essere giù di corda* (feel down), *essere al settimo cielo* (be over the moon), *cadere dalle nuvole* (be taken completely by surprise; lit. 'fall from the clouds').

examples.it: Non vedo l'ora di rivederti!
examples.en: I can't wait to see you again!

examples.it: Oggi lascialo stare: ha un diavolo per capello.
examples.en: Leave him alone today: he's furious.

rules.title: People
rules.text: *essere in gamba* (be capable, smart; lit. 'be in leg'), *essere un pezzo di pane* (be a sweetheart; lit. 'a piece of bread'), *non avere peli sulla lingua* (speak one's mind; lit. 'have no hairs on the tongue'), *avere la testa fra le nuvole* (be absent-minded), *essere una buona forchetta* (be a hearty eater; lit. 'a good fork'), *alla mano* (easy-going, down to earth).

examples.it: La nuova collega è molto in gamba.
examples.en: The new colleague is very capable.

examples.it: Mia nonna non ha peli sulla lingua.
examples.en: My grandmother doesn't mince her words.

rules.title: Situations and rituals
rules.text: *In bocca al lupo!* – *Crepi!* (Good luck! – lit. 'Into the wolf's mouth!' – 'May it die!'), *acqua in bocca* (keep it secret; lit. 'water in your mouth'), *fare le ore piccole* (stay up till the small hours), *ogni morte di papa* (once in a blue moon; lit. 'every time a pope dies'), *a occhio e croce* (roughly, at a guess), *in quattro e quattr'otto* (in no time). Register: *rompere le scatole* (get on someone's nerves) is fine with friends but rude at work.

examples.it: – Domani ho l'esame. – In bocca al lupo! – Crepi!
examples.en: – I've got my exam tomorrow. – Good luck! – Thanks!

examples.it: A occhio e croce saremo in trenta.
examples.en: At a rough guess there'll be about thirty of us.

mistakes.why: 'Break a leg' doesn't exist in Italian.
*Grazie* is increasingly heard, but *Crepi (il lupo)!* is the traditional reply.
'Can't wait' is *non vedere l'ora di*. The literal version sounds like you're impatient for practical reasons.
Idioms are fixed: one devil for every single *capello*.

mistakes.wrong: Ci vediamo ogni morte di papà.
mistakes.right: Ci vediamo ogni morte di papa.
mistakes.why: *Papa* = pope; *papà* = dad. Watch the accent!

tips: Learn the literal image along with the meaning: a devil on every single hair makes 'furious' easy to remember.
Don't tweak idioms (number, article, preposition): they only work in their fixed form.
Check the register: *rompere le scatole* is fine with friends, never in a work email.

exercises.prompt: Your friend says: «In bocca al lupo per l'esame!» What's the traditional reply?

optionWhy.1: *Salute!* is what you say when someone sneezes.
optionWhy.2: *Anche a te* doesn't work: they're not the one taking the exam, and the ritual answer is *Crepi!*

exercises.explanation: *In bocca al lupo!* – *Crepi (il lupo)!* (lit. 'may the wolf die'). Some people now answer *Grazie* or *Viva il lupo*, but *Crepi!* is the classic.
exercises.en: Good luck with your exam! – Thanks!

exercises.prompt: Non posso venire in vacanza con voi, sono completamente al ___.
exercises.explanation: *Essere al verde* = be broke.
exercises.en: I can't come on holiday with you, I'm completely broke.

exercises.prompt: Non vedo l'___ di andare in vacanza!

traps.why: The idiom is fixed: *non vedere l'ora di*.

exercises.explanation: *Non vedere l'ora di* = can't wait to.
exercises.en: I can't wait to go on holiday!

exercises.prompt: Quella borsa è bellissima, ma costa un occhio della ___.
exercises.explanation: *Costare un occhio della testa* = cost an arm and a leg.
exercises.en: That bag is gorgeous, but it costs an arm and a leg.

exercises.prompt: «Marco ha le mani bucate.» This means:

optionWhy.0: Clumsy is *imbranato* or *ha le mani di burro* (butterfingers).

exercises.explanation: *Avere le mani bucate* = to be a spendthrift (money slips through the holes).
exercises.en: Marco spends money too easily.

exercises.prompt: Il nonno di Sara è buonissimo, un vero pezzo di ___.
exercises.explanation: *Essere un pezzo di pane* = be a kind, gentle person.
exercises.en: Sara's grandfather is lovely, a real sweetheart.

exercises.prompt: I can't wait to see you!

traps.why: 'Can't wait to' = *non vedere l'ora di*. *Non posso aspettare* is a literal calque.

exercises.explanation: *Non vedere l'ora di* + infinitive.
exercises.en: I can't wait to see you!

exercises.prompt: Oggi non parlargli del lavoro: ha un diavolo per ___.

traps.why: The idiom is fixed in the singular: *un diavolo per capello* (one devil for each hair).

exercises.explanation: *Avere un diavolo per capello* = be furious.
exercises.en: Don't talk to him about work today: he's absolutely furious.

exercises.prompt: «Ti dico una cosa, ma acqua in bocca!» means:
exercises.explanation: *Acqua in bocca* = keep it secret, don't tell anyone.
exercises.en: I'll tell you something, but keep it to yourself!

exercises.instruction: Which sentence would be out of place in a formal email to your boss?
exercises.prompt: Choose the inappropriate sentence.
options: Resto a disposizione per qualsiasi chiarimento.
Mi sta rompendo le scatole con questa storia.

optionWhy.0: This is a standard formal closing.

exercises.explanation: *Rompere le scatole* (get on someone's nerves) is informal and rude in a work context.
exercises.en: He's getting on my nerves with this business.

exercises.instruction: Rewrite using the idiom 'non avere peli sulla lingua'.
exercises.prompt: Mia sorella dice sempre quello che pensa, senza filtri.
answers: Mia sorella non ha peli sulla lingua

traps.why: The idiom is plural: *non avere peli sulla lingua*.
The idiom uses *sulla*: *peli sulla lingua*.

exercises.explanation: *Non avere peli sulla lingua* = speak one's mind, not mince one's words.
exercises.en: My sister always says what she thinks.

exercises.prompt: Quando gli abbiamo detto che ci sposavamo, è caduto dalle ___: non ne sapeva niente.

traps.why: The idiom is *cadere dalle nuvole* (from the clouds).
The fixed form is *nuvole*.

exercises.explanation: *Cadere dalle nuvole* = be completely taken by surprise.
exercises.en: When we told him we were getting married, he was stunned: he knew nothing about it.

exercises.prompt: It cost an arm and a leg.

traps.why: The Italian image is different: *costare un occhio della testa*.

exercises.explanation: *Costare un occhio della testa* = cost a fortune.
exercises.en: It cost an arm and a leg.

exercises.prompt: «Ieri abbiamo fatto le ore piccole.» This means:
exercises.explanation: *Fare le ore piccole* = stay up until the small hours.
exercises.en: Yesterday we stayed up very late.

exercises.prompt: Si vede che oggi è giù di ___: non ha detto una parola.

traps.why: *Essere giù di morale* also exists, but the fixed idiom here is *giù di corda*.

exercises.explanation: *Essere giù di corda* = feel down, low.
exercises.en: You can tell he's feeling down today: he hasn't said a word.

exercises.prompt: Your friend is going to a job interview. Wish them luck the Italian way.
answers: In bocca al lupo[ per il colloquio]
In bocca al lupo per il tuo colloquio

traps.why: 'Break a leg' doesn't exist in Italian. Say *In bocca al lupo!*
*Buona fortuna* is fine, but the idiomatic wish is *In bocca al lupo!*

exercises.explanation: *In bocca al lupo!* is the standard good-luck wish before exams and interviews.
exercises.en: Good luck (with the interview)!

exercises.prompt: He's really capable, but he always has his head in the clouds.
answers: È (davvero|molto|proprio|veramente) in gamba[,] ma ha sempre la testa (fra|tra) le nuvole
È (davvero|molto|proprio|veramente) in gamba[,] ma è sempre (fra|tra) le nuvole
È (davvero|molto|proprio|veramente) in gamba[,] ma è sempre con la testa (fra|tra) le nuvole

traps.why: Italian uses *nuvole* (clouds) for absent-mindedness: *avere la testa fra le nuvole*.
*Capace* is correct, but *in gamba* is the idiomatic choice.

exercises.explanation: *Essere in gamba* = be capable; *avere la testa fra le nuvole* = be absent-minded.
exercises.en: He's really capable, but he always has his head in the clouds.

exercises.prompt: Ci vediamo ogni morte di ___: l'ultima volta è stata tre anni fa!

traps.why: *Papà* (accent) means dad! The idiom is about the Pope: *ogni morte di papa*.

exercises.explanation: *Ogni morte di papa* = once in a blue moon.
exercises.en: We see each other once in a blue moon: the last time was three years ago!

concepts.title: Advanced idioms and proverbs
concepts.rule: Advanced idioms and proverbs are fixed and often quoted in half: prendere due piccioni con una fava, fare orecchie da mercante, cadere a fagiolo, chi va piano va sano e va lontano, tutto fa brodo. Know the image, the meaning and the register.
assessment: Recognises common proverbs from their first half and explains their meaning
Matches idioms and proverbs to situations
Uses advanced idioms in their fixed form, including old words (piglia, menare, can)
Uses proverbs with the right register, often with a touch of irony

lesson.intro: Proverbs and colourful idioms are everywhere in Italian journalism, TV and family conversation, often shortened (*Chi dorme…*) or twisted for effect. At C1 you need to recognise them from a fragment, understand the allusion, and drop the occasional one into speech or writing at the right moment, usually with a hint of irony.

rules.title: Efficiency and opportunity
rules.text: *prendere due piccioni con una fava* (kill two birds with one stone; lit. 'catch two pigeons with one broad bean'), *cadere / capitare a fagiolo* (come at just the right moment), *tutto fa brodo* (every little helps; lit. 'everything makes broth'), *chi dorme non piglia pesci* (the early bird catches the worm; lit. 'whoever sleeps catches no fish'), *meglio un uovo oggi che una gallina domani* (a bird in the hand is worth two in the bush), *salvare capra e cavoli* (have it both ways; lit. 'save the goat and the cabbages').

examples.it: Passo in banca e poi dal medico: prendo due piccioni con una fava.
examples.en: I'll stop at the bank and then the doctor's: two birds, one stone.

examples.it: Il tuo aiuto è caduto proprio a fagiolo.
examples.en: Your help came at exactly the right moment.

rules.title: Behaviour and character
rules.text: *fare orecchie da mercante* (turn a deaf ear; lit. 'have merchant's ears'), *menare il can per l'aia* (beat around the bush; lit. 'lead the dog around the threshing floor'), *avere la coda di paglia* (have a guilty conscience; lit. 'a straw tail', which catches fire easily), *il lupo perde il pelo ma non il vizio* (a leopard never changes its spots), *non è farina del tuo sacco* (it's not your own work), *fare di tutta l'erba un fascio* (tar everyone with the same brush), *l'abito non fa il monaco* (don't judge a book by its cover).

examples.it: Gli ho chiesto i soldi tre volte, ma fa orecchie da mercante.
examples.en: I've asked him for the money three times, but he turns a deaf ear.

examples.it: Non tutti i politici sono corrotti: non fare di tutta l'erba un fascio.
examples.en: Not all politicians are corrupt: don't tar them all with the same brush.

rules.title: Plans and outcomes
rules.text: *chi va piano va sano e va lontano* (slow and steady wins the race), *tra il dire e il fare c'è di mezzo il mare* (easier said than done), *non tutte le ciambelle riescono col buco* (things don't always turn out as planned; lit. 'not every ring cake comes out with a hole'), *dalla padella nella brace* (out of the frying pan into the fire), *tagliare la testa al toro* (settle the matter once and for all), *gettare la spugna* (throw in the towel), *chi la fa l'aspetti* (what goes around comes around).

examples.it: Ho cambiato lavoro e il nuovo capo è peggio: dalla padella nella brace!
examples.en: I changed jobs and the new boss is worse: out of the frying pan into the fire!

examples.it: Per tagliare la testa al toro, decidiamo a maggioranza.
examples.en: To settle it once and for all, let's decide by majority vote.

rules.title: How proverbs are used
rules.text: Proverbs are often quoted in half (*Chi va piano…*, *Tra il dire e il fare…*) because everyone knows the ending. They're neutral to informal: in formal writing use them sparingly, introduced by *come dice il proverbio* or *come si suol dire*. Some keep old words: *pigliare* (= prendere), *menare* (= condurre), *can* (= cane).

examples.it: Come si suol dire, tra il dire e il fare c'è di mezzo il mare.
examples.en: As they say, it's easier said than done.

examples.it: Eh, chi dorme…
examples.en: Well, you snooze, you lose…

mistakes.wrong: Prendere due uccelli con una pietra.
mistakes.right: Prendere due piccioni con una fava.
mistakes.why: Don't translate the English image: Italian uses pigeons and a broad bean.
*Fare il sordo* exists, but the idiom is *orecchie da mercante*.
Fixed form: singular *fagiolo*.

mistakes.wrong: Il lupo perde il vizio ma non il pelo.
mistakes.right: Il lupo perde il pelo ma non il vizio.
mistakes.why: The wolf loses its fur (it gets old) but keeps its bad habits.

tips: Learn the second half: when you hear *Chi la fa…* you should be able to finish it (*…l'aspetti*).
Use a proverb to round off an anecdote, not to open a formal essay.
Ironic twists (*Chi va piano… arriva tardi*) only work if you know the original: recognise both.

exercises.prompt: Vado in centro a pagare la bolletta e intanto passo da mia madre: prendo due piccioni con una ___.

optionWhy.1: That's the English image (one stone). Italian uses *una fava* (a broad bean).
optionWhy.2: Italian uses *una fava*, not a stone.

exercises.explanation: *Prendere due piccioni con una fava* = kill two birds with one stone.
exercises.en: I'm going into town to pay the bill and I'll stop at my mother's: two birds with one stone.

exercises.prompt: We killed two birds with one stone.
answers: Abbiamo preso due piccioni con una fava
exercises.explanation: The idiom is fixed: *prendere due piccioni con una fava*.
exercises.en: We killed two birds with one stone.

exercises.prompt: Gli ho chiesto tre volte di restituirmi i soldi, ma lui fa orecchie da ___.

traps.why: *Fare il sordo* exists, but the idiom is *fare orecchie da mercante*.

exercises.explanation: *Fare orecchie da mercante* = turn a deaf ear, pretend not to hear.
exercises.en: I've asked him three times to give me my money back, but he turns a deaf ear.

exercises.prompt: La tua telefonata è caduta a ___: stavo proprio per chiamarti!
exercises.explanation: *Cadere / capitare a fagiolo* = come at exactly the right moment.
exercises.en: Your call came at just the right moment: I was about to ring you!

exercises.prompt: Non avere fretta: chi va piano va sano e va ___.
exercises.explanation: *Chi va piano va sano e va lontano* = slow and steady wins the race.
exercises.en: Don't rush: slow and steady wins the race.

exercises.prompt: La torta è venuta un disastro… Pazienza: non tutte le ciambelle riescono col ___.
exercises.explanation: *Non tutte le ciambelle riescono col buco* = things don't always turn out as planned.
exercises.en: The cake was a disaster… Oh well: you can't win them all.

exercises.prompt: The teacher says: «Questo tema non è farina del tuo sacco.» She means:
options: This essay isn't your cup of tea.
You didn't write this essay yourself.
exercises.explanation: *Non è farina del tuo sacco* = it's not your own work (lit. 'not flour from your sack').
exercises.en: You didn't write this essay yourself.

exercises.prompt: Non è un grande guadagno, ma tutto fa ___.
exercises.explanation: *Tutto fa brodo* = every little helps (lit. 'everything makes broth').
exercises.en: It's not a big profit, but every little helps.

exercises.prompt: Every little helps.

traps.why: The Italian idiom uses a cooking image: *tutto fa brodo*.

exercises.explanation: *Tutto fa brodo* is the idiomatic equivalent.
exercises.en: Every little helps.

exercises.instruction: Replace the sentence with the proverb that means 'you snooze, you lose' (Chi dorme…).
exercises.prompt: Se ti alzi tardi, perdi le occasioni migliori.

traps.why: Understood and sometimes heard, but the canonical form keeps the old verb: *piglia*.

exercises.explanation: *Chi dorme non piglia pesci* (*pigliare* = colloquial/old *prendere*).
exercises.en: The early bird catches the worm.

exercises.prompt: «Non fare di tutta l'erba un fascio.» means:
options: Don't put all your eggs in one basket.
Don't generalise; don't tar everyone with the same brush.

optionWhy.0: That's *non mettere tutte le uova nello stesso paniere*.

exercises.explanation: *Fare di tutta l'erba un fascio* = lump everything together, generalise unfairly.
exercises.en: Don't tar everyone with the same brush.

exercises.prompt: Ha giurato che avrebbe smesso di giocare d'azzardo, ma il lupo perde il pelo ma non il ___.
exercises.explanation: *Il lupo perde il pelo ma non il vizio* = a leopard never changes its spots.
exercises.en: He swore he'd stop gambling, but a leopard never changes its spots.

exercises.prompt: «Smettila di menare il can per l'aia e dimmi cosa è successo!»
options: Stop walking the dog and tell me what happened!
Stop beating around the bush and tell me what happened!
Stop exaggerating and tell me what happened!

optionWhy.0: The literal image is about a dog, but the meaning is figurative.

exercises.explanation: *Menare il can per l'aia* = beat around the bush, stall.
exercises.en: Stop beating around the bush and tell me what happened!

exercises.prompt: Luca promised to finish renovating the house in a month. A year later it's still not done. Which proverb fits?
options: Tra il dire e il fare c'è di mezzo il mare.
Chi va piano va sano e va lontano.

optionWhy.1: That praises slowness; here the point is the gap between promises and action.

exercises.explanation: *Tra il dire e il fare c'è di mezzo il mare* = easier said than done.
exercises.en: Easier said than done.

exercises.prompt: Ha proprio la coda di ___: appena ho parlato di furti, è diventato rosso.
exercises.explanation: *Avere la coda di paglia* = have a guilty conscience (a straw tail catches fire at the slightest spark).
exercises.en: He's got a guilty conscience: as soon as I mentioned thefts, he went red.

exercises.instruction: Translate using 'tagliare la testa al toro'.
exercises.prompt: Let's settle it once and for all: we'll split the costs.
answers: Tagliamo la testa al toro (dividiamo|ci dividiamo|divideremo|ci divideremo) (le spese|i costi)
Tagliamo la testa al toro facciamo a metà
Per tagliare la testa al toro (dividiamo|ci dividiamo|divideremo|ci divideremo) (le spese|i costi)

traps.why: *Prendere il toro per le corna* means facing a problem head-on. To settle a matter decisively: *tagliare la testa al toro*.

exercises.explanation: *Tagliare la testa al toro* = settle a matter decisively.
exercises.en: Let's settle it once and for all: we'll split the costs.

exercises.prompt: Your friend quit a terrible job, and the new one is even worse. Comment with the idiom for 'out of the frying pan into the fire'.
answers: È proprio il caso di dire dalla padella nella brace

traps.why: The Italian image ends in the embers: *dalla padella nella brace*.

exercises.explanation: *Cadere dalla padella nella brace* = go from bad to worse.
exercises.en: Out of the frying pan into the fire!

exercises.prompt: Complete the proverb: «Chi la fa…»
exercises.explanation: *Chi la fa l'aspetti* = what goes around comes around (whoever plays a dirty trick should expect one back).
exercises.en: What goes around comes around.

concepts.title: Word formation: prefixes, suffixes, altered nouns
concepts.rule: Prefixes (in-/im-/il-/ir-, s-, dis-, ri-) and suffixes (-mente, -zione, -mento, -tore/-trice, -ità, -ezza) build new words; altered nouns add size or attitude (-ino small, -one big, -accio bad). Beware false alterations like bottone, mattone, tacchino.
assessment: Forms opposites with the correct prefix (in-/im-/il-/ir-, s-, dis-)
Derives adverbs, nouns and feminine forms with the right suffix
Interprets altered nouns (-ino, -one, -accio, -astro) and their nuance
Recognises false and lexicalised alterations (bottone, tacchino, ombrellone)

lesson.intro: Italian builds vocabulary like Lego: a root plus prefixes and suffixes. Knowing the patterns lets you understand unfamiliar words instantly and produce the right adjective, noun or adverb when you need one. Altered nouns (*-ino, -one, -accio*) add nuances that English expresses with extra words (little, big, nasty).

rules.title: Negative and opposite prefixes
rules.text: **in-** becomes **im-** before *b, p, m*, **il-** before *l*, **ir-** before *r*: *inutile, impossibile, immaturo, illegale, irregolare*. **s-**: *scontento, scomodo, sfortunato, scorretto*. **dis-**: *disonesto, disoccupato, disattento, disordine*. **a-** (Greek): *asociale, apolitico*. Each word has its own prefix, so learn them as whole words.

examples.it: È impossibile parcheggiare qui.
examples.en: It's impossible to park here.

examples.it: Questa sedia è scomodissima.
examples.en: This chair is really uncomfortable.

rules.title: Verb prefixes
rules.text: **ri-** = again / back: *rifare, rileggere, ritornare*. **s-** = undo, remove: *scaricare* (unload), *scongelare* (defrost), *sbloccare* (unblock), *svitare* (unscrew). **dis-** = undo: *disfare* (unpack, undo), *disdire* (cancel a booking), *disattivare*.

examples.it: Hai scongelato il pesce?
examples.en: Have you defrosted the fish?

examples.it: Ho dovuto disdire l'appuntamento.
examples.en: I had to cancel the appointment.

rules.title: Suffixes that change the word class
rules.text: Adverbs: feminine adjective + **-mente** (*lento → lenta → lentamente*); adjectives in *-le / -re* drop the *-e* (*facile → facilmente, regolare → regolarmente*). Watch *leggero → leggermente*, *violento → violentemente*. Nouns from verbs: **-zione / -sione** (*organizzare → organizzazione, decidere → decisione*), **-mento** (*cambiare → cambiamento*), **-tore / -trice** (*lavoratore / lavoratrice, attore / attrice*; but *dottore → dottoressa*). Nouns from adjectives: **-ità** (*felice → felicità*), **-ezza** (*bello → bellezza*).

examples.it: Faccio sport regolarmente.
examples.en: I do sport regularly.

examples.it: L'organizzazione della festa è stata perfetta.
examples.en: The organisation of the party was perfect.

rules.title: Altered nouns: size and attitude
rules.text: **-ino, -etto, -ello**: small, cute (*gattino, casetta, alberello*). **-one**: big; feminine nouns often become masculine (*la porta → il portone*). **-accio**: bad, ugly, nasty (*tempaccio, parolaccia, ragazzaccio*). **-uccio**: small and endearing (*casuccia*). **-astro**: pejorative, or '-ish' with colours (*poetastro, giallastro*).

examples.it: Che tempaccio! Piove da tre giorni.
examples.en: What awful weather! It's been raining for three days.

examples.it: Aveva la pelle giallastra.
examples.en: His skin was an unhealthy yellowish colour.

rules.title: False alterations and lexicalised words
rules.text: Some words only look altered: *bottone* (button), *mattone* (brick), *burrone* (ravine), *tacchino* (turkey), *postino* (postman), *rubinetto* (tap), *focaccia*. Others started as alterations but are now separate words: *telefonino* (mobile phone), *ombrellone* (beach umbrella), *finestrino* (car or train window), *spazzolino* (toothbrush), *panino* (roll, sandwich).

examples.it: Mi si è staccato un bottone.
examples.en: A button has come off.

examples.it: Abbiamo affittato un ombrellone in prima fila.
examples.en: We rented a beach umbrella in the front row.

mistakes.why: *in-* assimilates: *im-* before p/b/m, *il-* before l, *ir-* before r.
*-mente* attaches to the feminine form: *lenta + mente*.
*Leggero* drops the final vowel: *leggermente*.
Masculine *-tore* → feminine *-trice*.
*-accio* is negative: a *giornataccia* is an awful day.

tips: Don't invent alterations freely in formal writing: many combinations don't exist, and many altered words are lexicalised.
When you meet a word ending in *-one* or *-ino*, check the dictionary before assuming it means 'big' or 'small'.
Use *-accio* and *-uccio* mainly in informal speech: they add attitude.

exercises.instruction: Form the opposite with a prefix.
exercises.prompt: È ___ (possibile → opposite) finire tutto in un giorno.

traps.why: *In-* becomes *im-* before p and b: *impossibile*.
The negative prefix here is *in-* → *im-*: *impossibile*.

exercises.explanation: *im-* before p: *impossibile*.
exercises.en: It's impossible to finish everything in one day.

exercises.instruction: Form an adverb in -mente from the adjective in brackets.
exercises.prompt: Parla più ___ (lento), per favore: non capisco.

traps.why: *-mente* attaches to the feminine form: *lenta → lentamente*.
In speech you'll hear *parla più lento*, but the task asks for the *-mente* adverb: *lentamente*.

exercises.explanation: Feminine adjective + *-mente*: *lentamente*.
exercises.en: Speak more slowly, please: I don't understand.

exercises.instruction: Give the feminine form of the word in brackets.
exercises.prompt: Mia figlia vuole fare l'___ (attore), come sua nonna.

traps.why: *-tore* → *-trice*: *attrice*.

exercises.explanation: *-tore → -trice*: *attore → attrice*.
exercises.en: My daughter wants to be an actress, like her grandmother.

exercises.instruction: Form the opposite with a prefix.
exercises.prompt: Vendere alcolici ai minorenni è ___ (legale → opposite).

traps.why: *In-* becomes *il-* before l: *illegale*.
Double l: *il- + legale = illegale*.

exercises.explanation: *il-* before l: *illegale*.
exercises.en: Selling alcohol to minors is illegal.

exercises.prompt: Che ___! Piove da tre giorni e fa freddo.

optionWhy.1: *-ino* is small/cute: it doesn't fit a complaint.
optionWhy.2: *Tempone* would mean 'big weather' and is used only jokingly for a great time.

exercises.explanation: *-accio* = bad, nasty: *tempaccio* = awful weather.
exercises.en: What awful weather! It's been raining and cold for three days.

exercises.prompt: Which word is NOT an altered form of another noun?
exercises.explanation: *Bottone* means 'button': it isn't a big *botto* (bang). A false alteration.
exercises.en: Which word is not an altered noun?

exercises.instruction: Form the word with a prefix (dis- + occupato).
exercises.prompt: Dopo la chiusura della fabbrica, Paolo è rimasto ___ (senza lavoro) per due anni.

traps.why: *Inoccupato* is someone who has never had a job. Paolo lost his job, so he's *disoccupato*.
Correct meaning, but the task asks for one word: *disoccupato*.

exercises.explanation: *Disoccupato* = unemployed (having lost a job).
exercises.en: After the factory closed, Paolo was unemployed for two years.

exercises.instruction: Form the opposite with a prefix.
exercises.prompt: È stato molto ___ (corretto → opposite) a non avvisarci.

traps.why: *Incorretto* is rare and old-fashioned. The everyday opposite of *corretto* is *scorretto*.
The prefix here is *s-*: *scorretto*.

exercises.explanation: *s-* + corretto = *scorretto* (unfair, improper).
exercises.en: It was very unfair of him not to warn us.

exercises.instruction: Rewrite using the noun formed from 'organizzare'.
exercises.prompt: Organizzare l'evento è stato difficile.

traps.why: Nouns from *-are* verbs often end in *-azione*: *organizzazione*.
*L'organizzazione* is feminine: *è stata difficile*.

exercises.explanation: *Organizzare → organizzazione* (feminine): *è stata*.
exercises.en: Organising the event was difficult.

exercises.instruction: Form an adverb in -mente from the adjective in brackets.
exercises.prompt: Sono arrivato ___ (leggero) in ritardo, scusate.

traps.why: *Leggero* is an exception: *leggermente*.

exercises.explanation: *Leggero* is irregular: it drops the vowel before *-mente*, giving *leggermente*.
exercises.en: I arrived slightly late, sorry.

exercises.prompt: «La pelle del malato era giallastra.» *Giallastra* means:
exercises.explanation: *-astro* with colours = '-ish', usually unpleasant: *giallastro, verdastro*.
exercises.en: The patient's skin was yellowish.

exercises.instruction: Form the verb with a prefix meaning 'undo' (… + caricare).
exercises.prompt: Il camion ha ___ la merce davanti al magazzino.

traps.why: The reversing prefix here is *s-*: *scaricare*.
*Caricare* = load. Unload = *scaricare*.

exercises.explanation: *s-* reverses: *caricare → scaricare* (unload).
exercises.en: The lorry unloaded the goods in front of the warehouse.

exercises.prompt: The postman left a little parcel by the main front door.
answers: Il postino ha lasciato un (pacchetto|pacchettino) (davanti al|vicino al|accanto al) portone
Il postino ha lasciato (davanti al|vicino al|accanto al) portone un (pacchetto|pacchettino)

traps.why: The big main door of a building is *il portone* (porta + -one, masculine).
The postman is *il postino*.

exercises.explanation: *Postino* (postman), *pacchetto* (small parcel), *portone* (main door of a building).
exercises.en: The postman left a little parcel by the main front door.

exercises.prompt: What is a *tacchino*?
exercises.explanation: *Tacchino* = turkey: a false alteration, not 'small *tacco*'.
exercises.en: A turkey.

exercises.instruction: Form the opposite with a prefix.
exercises.prompt: Mia sorella è molto ___ (attenta → opposite): perde sempre le chiavi.

traps.why: The standard opposite of *attento* is *disattento*.

exercises.explanation: *dis-* + attenta = *disattenta* (careless, absent-minded).
exercises.en: My sister is very careless: she's always losing her keys.

exercises.instruction: Use an altered form of 'parola' (bad words).
exercises.prompt: Non dire ___ davanti ai bambini!

traps.why: *Paroloni* are big, pompous words. Swear words are *parolacce* (-accia = bad).
*Paroline* are sweet little words. Swear words are *parolacce*.

exercises.explanation: *Parola + -accia → parolaccia* = swear word.
exercises.en: Don't swear in front of the children!

exercises.instruction: Replace 'in modo regolare' with a single adverb.
exercises.prompt: Faccio sport in modo regolare.

traps.why: Adjectives in *-re* drop the *-e*: *regolarmente*.

exercises.explanation: *-le / -re* adjectives drop the final *-e* before *-mente*.
exercises.en: I do sport regularly.

exercises.prompt: Al mare abbiamo affittato due lettini e un ___.

optionWhy.0: An *ombrellino* is a small umbrella or parasol you carry.
optionWhy.2: *Ombrellaccio* is an ugly or broken umbrella.

exercises.explanation: *Ombrellone* is a lexicalised word: beach umbrella.
exercises.en: At the beach we rented two sunloungers and a beach umbrella.

concepts.title: Argumentation and academic vocabulary
concepts.rule: Formal argument uses a fixed toolkit: sostenere / ribadire / evidenziare to state, confutare / smentire / contestare to challenge, ne consegue che / pertanto to conclude, alla luce di / in merito a to frame. Beware evidenza (≠ evidence) and assumere (= hire).
assessment: Uses varied verbs to report and evaluate claims (sostenere, ribadire, evidenziare, confutare)
Signals consequence and contrast with formal connectors (ne consegue che, pertanto, ciononostante)
Frames arguments with expressions such as *alla luce di*, *in merito a*, *a fronte di*
Avoids academic false friends (evidenza, assumere, discutere che)
Writes a short structured argument in a formal register

lesson.intro: At C1 you are expected to argue: present a thesis, support it, deal with objections and draw conclusions. Italian academic and journalistic prose relies on a fairly fixed toolkit of verbs (*sostenere, ribadire, evidenziare, confutare*) and framing phrases (*alla luce di, ne consegue che*). Several English-looking words are traps here: *evidenza*, *assumere*, *discutere*, *controllare*.

rules.title: Presenting and reinforcing a position
rules.text: *sostenere che* (argue, maintain), *affermare* (state), *ribadire* (reiterate), *sottolineare / evidenziare / mettere in luce* (highlight), *rilevare* (note, point out). After *sostenere che* you'll find both moods: the indicative presents the claim as fact, the subjunctive keeps a critical distance.

examples.it: L'autrice sostiene che il lavoro da remoto aumenti la produttività.
examples.en: The author argues that remote work increases productivity.

examples.it: Il ministro ha ribadito che non ci saranno nuove tasse.
examples.en: The minister reiterated that there will be no new taxes.

rules.title: Challenging a position
rules.text: *confutare* (refute, with arguments), *smentire* (deny, disprove: rumours, news), *contestare* (dispute), *obiettare* (object), *mettere in discussione / in dubbio* (call into question).

examples.it: Lo studio confuta la tesi tradizionale.
examples.en: The study refutes the traditional thesis.

examples.it: Il portavoce ha smentito la notizia.
examples.en: The spokesperson denied the report.

rules.title: Logic: cause and consequence
rules.text: *ne consegue che / ne deriva che* (it follows that), *di conseguenza*, *pertanto*, *dunque* (therefore), *ciò comporta* (this entails), *dal momento che*, *in quanto* (since, as). For contrast: *tuttavia*, *ciononostante*, *d'altro canto*.

examples.it: I costi sono aumentati; ne consegue che il progetto va rivisto.
examples.en: Costs have risen; it follows that the project must be revised.

examples.it: Il campione è ridotto, pertanto i risultati vanno presi con cautela.
examples.en: The sample is small, therefore the results must be treated with caution.

rules.title: Framing and structuring
rules.text: *alla luce di* (in light of), *in merito a / per quanto riguarda / quanto a* (regarding), *a fronte di* (in the face of, against), *nell'ambito di* (within), *in base a* (based on), *va detto che* (it should be said), *in sintesi / in conclusione*.

examples.it: Alla luce di questi dati, è necessario un cambio di rotta.
examples.en: In light of these data, a change of course is needed.

examples.it: A fronte di un aumento dei costi, i salari sono rimasti fermi.
examples.en: Against a rise in costs, wages have stayed flat.

rules.title: Academic false friends

head: Italian
means
for the English word, say
rows: hire; take on (a role, a responsibility)

rules.text: In scientific jargon *evidenze* (evidence) is spreading as an anglicism; in general Italian use *prove*.

examples.it: Non ci sono prove che il farmaco funzioni.
examples.en: There is no evidence that the drug works.

examples.it: Per eventuali domande, scrivete alla segreteria.
examples.en: For any questions, write to the office.

mistakes.right: Non ci sono prove che funzioni.
mistakes.why: *Evidenza* means obviousness. Evidence = *prove*.

mistakes.wrong: Assumiamo che i dati siano corretti.
mistakes.right: Supponiamo che i dati siano corretti.
mistakes.why: *Assumere* mainly means 'hire' or 'take on'. For 'assume' use *supporre* or *presumere*.
The fixed phrase is *alla luce di*.

mistakes.wrong: L'autore discute che il turismo danneggia la città.
mistakes.right: L'autore sostiene che il turismo danneggi la città.
mistakes.why: *Discutere* = discuss, not 'argue that'.

tips: Build a personal kit of two verbs per function (state, reinforce, object, conclude) and rotate them so you never repeat *dire*.
Formal Italian loves prepositional phrases: *alla luce di*, *a fronte di*, *in merito a*, *nell'ambito di*.
Don't overdo it in conversation: *quindi* and *però* are perfectly fine when speaking.

exercises.prompt: Il ministro ha ___ (reiterated) che non ci saranno nuove tasse.

traps.why: *Ripetere* is correct but neutral. *Ribadire* (reiterate, stress again) is the typical formal choice.
*Reiterare* exists but is very formal and usually takes a noun (*reiterare una richiesta*). With *che*, use *ribadire*.

exercises.explanation: *Ribadire* = reiterate, restate firmly.
exercises.en: The minister reiterated that there will be no new taxes.

exercises.prompt: Gli autori ___ la tesi secondo cui il clima non influisce sulle migrazioni.
exercises.explanation: *Confutare* = refute with arguments.
exercises.en: The authors refute the thesis that climate doesn't affect migration.

exercises.prompt: ___ luce di questi risultati, dobbiamo rivedere il progetto.

traps.why: The fixed phrase is *alla luce di* (in light of).
The fixed phrase is *alla luce di*.

exercises.explanation: *Alla luce di* = in light of.
exercises.en: In light of these results, we must revise the project.

exercises.prompt: «L'azienda ha assunto dieci ingegneri.» This means the company…
exercises.explanation: *Assumere* = hire; also take on (*assumersi una responsabilità*).
exercises.en: The company hired ten engineers.

exercises.prompt: I primi risultati sono positivi; ne ___ che la strategia funziona.

traps.why: *Ne risulta* is possible in some contexts, but the fixed formula for 'it follows that' is *ne consegue che*.

exercises.explanation: *Ne consegue che* / *ne deriva che* = it follows that.
exercises.en: The first results are positive; it follows that the strategy works.

exercises.prompt: I dati sono incoraggianti. ___, il campione è troppo piccolo per trarre conclusioni.

optionWhy.0: *Pertanto* introduces a consequence, not a contrast.

exercises.explanation: *Ciononostante* = nevertheless.
exercises.en: The data are encouraging. Nevertheless, the sample is too small to draw conclusions.

exercises.instruction: Rewrite in a more formal style, starting with 'Rossi sostiene che…'.
exercises.prompt: Secondo Rossi, il progetto è troppo costoso.
answers: Rossi sostiene che il progetto (sia|è) troppo costoso

traps.why: *Dire* is neutral; the task asks for *sostenere*.

exercises.explanation: *Sostenere che* + subjunctive (critical distance) or indicative (presented as fact). Both are used.
exercises.en: Rossi maintains that the project is too expensive.

exercises.prompt: There is no evidence that the drug works.
answers: Non ci sono prove che il farmaco funzioni
Non esistono prove che il farmaco funzioni
Non c'è (nessuna|alcuna) prova che il farmaco funzioni

traps.why: *Non ci sono prove che* expresses doubt, so it takes the subjunctive: *funzioni*.
*Evidenza* means 'obviousness'. Evidence = *prove*.
*Evidenze* is common in scientific jargon (an anglicism). In general Italian, prefer *prove*.

exercises.explanation: Evidence = *prove*; *non ci sono prove che* + subjunctive.
exercises.en: There is no evidence that the drug works.

exercises.prompt: Una nuova ricerca ha ___ le voci su un legame tra telefoni cellulari e tumori.

traps.why: *Negare* is what a person does (deny). Research that disproves rumours *smentisce* them.
*Rifiutare* = refuse, reject (an offer). Disprove = *smentire*.

exercises.explanation: *Smentire* = disprove, deny (rumours, reports).
exercises.en: New research has disproved the rumours of a link between mobile phones and cancer.

exercises.prompt: In light of the data, we can conclude that the plan has failed.
answers: Alla luce dei dati[,] (possiamo|si può) concludere che il (piano|progetto) (è fallito|non ha funzionato)

traps.why: The fixed phrase is *alla luce di*.
A plan fails with *essere*: *il piano è fallito*. (*Ha fallito* is for a person failing at something: *ha fallito l'esame*.)

exercises.explanation: *Alla luce di* + *concludere che* + indicative; *fallire* (of a plan) takes *essere*.
exercises.en: In light of the data, we can conclude that the plan has failed.

exercises.prompt: Vorrei ___ (to stress) un aspetto fondamentale: la sicurezza dei dati.

traps.why: *Stressare* means to stress someone out. To emphasise = *sottolineare*.
*Accentuare* = accentuate, intensify (a feature). To stress a point = *sottolineare*.

exercises.explanation: Stress a point = *sottolineare / evidenziare*.
exercises.en: I'd like to stress one fundamental aspect: data security.

exercises.prompt: It follows that the model must be revised.
answers: Ne consegue che il modello va rivisto
exercises.explanation: *Ne consegue che* opens the sentence; *va rivisto* = must be revised (passive with *andare*).
exercises.en: It follows that the model must be revised.

exercises.instruction: Choose the best opening for the conclusion of a formal essay.
exercises.prompt: Which sentence fits?
options: In sintesi, i dati raccolti confermano l'ipotesi iniziale.
Insomma, alla fine i dati dicono che avevo ragione.
Comunque sia, boh, i dati confermano.

optionWhy.1: *Insomma, alla fine* and *avevo ragione* are conversational.

exercises.explanation: *In sintesi / In conclusione* + impersonal statement is the expected academic register.
exercises.en: In summary, the data collected confirm the initial hypothesis.

exercises.instruction: Fill the gap with an expression meaning 'with regard to'.
exercises.prompt: ___ la seconda obiezione, va detto che i costi sono già stati ridotti.

traps.why: Use *riguardo a* (with *a*) or *per quanto riguarda*.
'With respect to' is *rispetto a* or *per quanto riguarda*, without *con*.

exercises.explanation: *Per quanto riguarda / in merito a / quanto a* = as regards.
exercises.en: As regards the second objection, it should be said that costs have already been reduced.

exercises.prompt: The author argues that tourism damages the city.
answers: (L'autore|L'autrice) sostiene che il turismo (danneggi|danneggia) la città
(L'autore|L'autrice) sostiene che il turismo (rechi|reca|arrechi|arreca) danno alla città

traps.why: *Discutere* = discuss (or quarrel). 'Argue that' = *sostenere che*.
*Argomentare* exists in formal Italian, but *sostenere che* is the standard way to say 'argue that'.
*Litigare* = to quarrel. 'Argue that' = *sostenere che*.
